tool.name: Focaloop VariationLoop
tool.description: call genomic variants (SNVs and indels) across cohorts or single samples from paired FASTQ collections, BAM, indexed CRAM, or Logan unitigs
tool.command: FOCALOOP_DEDUP_MODE='$calling_options.dedup' focaloop variationloop --analysis-mode 'auto' #if str($ref_source.source) == "cached" --ref-fasta '$ref_source.cached_fasta.fields.path' --reference-label '${str($ref_source.cached_fasta.fields.name).replace("'", "_")}' #elif str($ref_source.source) == "history" --ref-fasta '$ref_source.ref_fasta' --reference-label '${str($ref_source.ref_fasta.element_identifier).replace("'", "_")}' #else --ncbi-accession '${str($ref_source.ncbi_accession).strip()}' --reference-label '${str($ref_source.ncbi_accession).strip()}' #end if #if str($input_source.source_type) == "history_paired_list" --reads-r1 #for $pair in $input_source.paired_reads '$pair.forward' #end for --reads-r2 #for $pair in $input_source.paired_reads '$pair.reverse' #end for --read-ids #for $pair in $input_source.paired_reads '${(str($pair.element_identifier).replace("'", "_").lstrip("-") or "sample")}' #end for #if $input_source.group_sheet --manifest '$input_source.group_sheet' #end if --logan-mode 'off' #elif str($input_source.source_type) == "history_bam" --bam #for $b in $input_source.bam '$b' #end for --bam-ids #for $b in $input_source.bam '${(str($b.element_identifier).replace("'", "_").lstrip("-") or "sample")}' #end for --crai #for $idx, $b in enumerate($input_source.bam) #if $idx == 0 and $input_source.crai '$input_source.crai' #elif $b.is_of_type("cram") and str($b.metadata.cram_index) not in ("", "None") '$b.metadata.cram_index' #elif $b.is_of_type("bam") and str($b.metadata.bam_index) not in ("", "None") '$b.metadata.bam_index' #else '' #end if #end for #if $input_source.group_sheet --manifest '$input_source.group_sheet' #end if --logan-mode 'off' #else #if str($input_source.sra_input.mode) == "manifest" --manifest '$input_source.sra_input.manifest' #else --manifest '$inline_var_manifest_tsv' #end if --logan-mode '$input_source.logan_mode' #end if --ploidy '$calling_model.ploidy' #if str($calling_model.ploidy) == "haploid" --min-wsaf $calling_model.min_wsaf #else --min-wsaf $streaming_options.logan_min_wsaf #end if #if $targets_bed --targets-bed '$targets_bed' #end if --host-depletion-mode '$streaming_options.host_depletion_mode' --logan-min-ka '$streaming_options.logan_min_ka' --cram-pad-bp $streaming_options.cram_pad_bp --subsample-fraction $streaming_options.subsample_fraction --mapper '$streaming_options.mapper' $calling_options.reassembly --min-mapq $calling_options.min_mapq --min-bq $calling_options.min_bq --snv-min-qual $calling_options.snv_min_qual --indel-min-qual $calling_options.indel_min_qual #if str($calling_options.dedup) == "off" --dedup-bits 0 #end if @THREADS@ --state-dir variationloop_state_dir --state-archive '$variationloop_state' --out-variants '$variants_summary' --out-vcf '$variants_vcf' --out-report '$variationloop_report'

param.label: Reference genome source
param.help: Choose a reference genome pre-cached on this Galaxy server, a FASTA dataset from your History, or an NCBI assembly accession to download automatically.
param.option: Built-in Galaxy genome (CVMFS cache)
Reference genome from your Galaxy History (FASTA)
Fetch automatically by NCBI assembly accession

param.name: cached_fasta
param.label: Built-in reference genome
param.help: Select a reference genome pre-cached on this Galaxy server.

validator.message: No built-in genomes are cached on this Galaxy server. Switch Reference genome source to History or NCBI accession.

param.label: Reference genome (FASTA)
param.help: Reference genome assembly matching your reads or alignment files (uncompressed or gzip-compressed).

param.label: NCBI assembly accession
param.help: RefSeq (GCF_ prefix) or GenBank (GCA_ prefix) assembly accession. The genomic FASTA is downloaded automatically.

validator.message: Enter an NCBI assembly accession starting with GCF_ or GCA_.
Enter a valid NCBI RefSeq (GCF_) or GenBank (GCA_) assembly accession with 9 digits and optional version.

param.name: source_type
param.label: Sequencing input source
param.help: Call variants across a paired-end FASTQ collection (one or more samples), aligned BAM/CRAM file(s), or public SRA/ENA runs and remote cohort manifests. Sample names in VCF headers and reports are derived automatically from your Galaxy collection/dataset names, run accessions, or manifest.
param.option: Galaxy History paired-end FASTQ collection (list:paired)
Galaxy History aligned BAM or CRAM file(s)
Public SRA/ENA run accessions or remote cohort manifest (Logan unitigs or raw streaming)

param.name: paired_reads
param.label: Paired-end FASTQ collection (list:paired)
param.help: Galaxy list-of-pairs collection containing one or more samples. Each pair's element identifier becomes its sample name in the VCF (merged across all samples for cohorts), summary table, HTML report, and saved state bundle.

param.name: group_sheet
param.label: Population or group metadata sheet (TSV or CSV, optional)
param.help: Optional table with sample_id and group (or population) columns matching collection element identifiers. Leave empty if you do not need group labels for downstream Focaloop Query comparisons.

param.label: Aligned reads (one or more BAM or CRAM datasets)
param.help: Coordinate-sorted BAM or CRAM file(s) aligned to the selected reference genome (accepts a single dataset, multiple datasets, or a list collection). Dataset names become sample names automatically. Indexed CRAM inputs automatically use compressed-block region slicing.

param.label: Explicit alignment index override (.crai or .bai, optional)
param.help: Leave empty to use the index Galaxy already tracks for each BAM or CRAM dataset. Supply an explicit .crai file only when providing a single unindexed CRAM dataset.

param.name: group_sheet
param.label: Population or group metadata sheet (TSV or CSV, optional)
param.help: Optional table with sample_id and group (or population) columns matching BAM/CRAM dataset names for downstream Focaloop Query group comparisons.

param.name: mode
param.label: How to specify public runs or remote files
param.help: Paste a flat list of public SRA/ENA accessions, organize accessions into population or condition groups inline for downstream Focaloop Query comparisons, or upload a cohort TSV/CSV manifest (supports remote CRAM+CRAI and FASTQ URLs).
param.option: Flat list of public SRA/ENA run accession(s)
Enter population or condition groups and run accessions directly (inline builder)
Cohort manifest from Galaxy History (TSV or CSV)

param.label: Public SRA/ENA run accession(s)
param.help: Enter one or more public SRA/ENA run accessions (SRR, ERR, or DRR prefix) separated by newlines, spaces, or commas. Each run accession becomes its sample name automatically.

Enter public SRA/ENA run accessions (SRR, ERR, or DRR prefix) separated by newlines, spaces, or commas.

repeat.help: Define one or more sample groups (for example, resistant and sensitive, or site populations) and list the public SRA/ENA run accessions belonging to each group. Group labels are saved in the cohort state bundle for downstream Focaloop Query Fst and allele-frequency comparisons.

param.name: group_name
param.label: Group or population name
param.help: Short group label (letters, digits, underscores, dots, or hyphens only, for example resistant or sensitive).

Use letters, digits, underscores, dots, or hyphens only.

param.name: accessions
param.label: Public SRA/ENA run accessions
param.help: Enter one or more public SRA/ENA run accessions (SRR, ERR, or DRR prefix) separated by newlines, spaces, or commas.

validator.message: Enter at least one public SRA/ENA run accession for this group.
Enter public SRA/ENA run accessions (SRR, ERR, or DRR prefix) separated by newlines, spaces, or commas.

param.label: Cohort manifest (TSV or CSV)
param.help: Table with required columns sample_id, group, and source (public SRA/ENA run accession, remote CRAM URL, or remote FASTQ URL), plus optional crai_uri (for remote CRAMs) or mate2_url (for remote paired FASTQs).

param.label: Pre-assembled Logan unitig streaming
param.help: When public SRA/ENA run accessions are available in the public Logan archive, VariationLoop can stream compact pre-assembled unitig graphs (~10-20x smaller than raw reads) and call variants directly.
param.option: Automatic (use Logan unitigs when available, fall back to raw reads otherwise)
Logan unitigs only (require pre-assembled Logan graphs for all runs)
Off (align raw reads or CRAM files only)

param.label: Calling model (organism ploidy)
param.help: Choose Haploid or mixed-clone (WSAF) for haploid organisms and polyclonal infections (such as haploid parasites, bacteria, viruses, or fungi) to call continuous within-sample allele fractions (GT=1 with per-sample FORMAT/WSAF) without imposing a 50/50 diploid genotype assumption. Choose Diploid for diploid organisms (such as human, vertebrates, or diploid eukaryotes) to emit standard 0/1, 1/1, and 1/2 genotypes alongside FORMAT/WSAF.
param.option: Diploid (0/1, 1/1, 1/2 genotypes - human, vertebrates, diploid eukaryotes)
Haploid or mixed-clone mixture (continuous WSAF, no diploid genotypes - haploid parasites, bacteria, viruses, fungi)

param.label: Minimum within-sample allele fraction (WSAF)
param.help: Minimum continuous alternate allele fraction required to report a variant in haploid or mixed-clone samples (default 0.25 balances precision and clonal sensitivity). Lower to 0.10-0.15 to detect minor clones in polyclonal infections, or raise to 0.50 for major-allele-only calls.

param.label: Target regions (BED, optional)
param.help: Optional 0-based BED intervals restricting variant calling, compressed CRAM region slicing, local haplotype reassembly, and host/off-target read pre-filtering to genes or panels of interest. Recommended for large genomes (> 45 Mb) when slicing CRAMs or filtering target reads.

param.label: Host and off-target read/unitig pre-filtering
param.help: Drops off-target or host reads/unitigs using a fast k-mer table built from your reference or BED targets before alignment (up to 50 Mb for Logan 15-mer filtering and 45 Mb for raw FASTQ 31-mer filtering).
param.option: Automatic (on for Logan unitigs up to 50 Mb and BED-targeted FASTQ up to 45 Mb, off for whole-genome FASTQ)
Always on (require target/reference span within k-mer memory limit)
Off (align all reads or unitigs directly)

param.label: Logan unitig k-mer abundance cutoff
param.help: Depth-adaptive mode calibrates the minimum unitig k-mer abundance (ka) automatically from each sample's coverage depth to balance sensitivity and error rejection (applies to Logan unitig runs only).
param.option: Depth-adaptive automatic cutoff (recommended)
Fixed minimum ka = 1.5 (sensitive, low-coverage samples)
Fixed minimum ka = 2.0 (balanced)
Fixed minimum ka = 3.0 (high-depth samples)

param.name: logan_min_wsaf
param.label: Minimum within-sample allele fraction (WSAF, diploid Logan unitigs)
param.help: Minimum weighted alternate allele fraction required when running Logan unitigs under Diploid mode (default 0.25). In Haploid mode, use the top-level Minimum within-sample allele fraction (WSAF) setting above.

param.label: Flanking padding around BED targets for CRAM slicing (bp)
param.help: Extra bases included on both sides of each BED interval when selecting compressed CRAM containers (applies to indexed CRAM inputs only).

param.label: Read subsampling fraction (raw FASTQ only, 1.0 = all reads)
param.help: Deterministically retains this fraction of paired FASTQ reads before alignment (ignored for BAM/CRAM and Logan unitig inputs). Leave at 1.0 to analyze every read.

param.label: Read and unitig aligner
param.help: Auto selects the fastest working aligner installed on the server (BWA-MEM2 preferred for Logan unitigs, strobealign/minimap2/BWA-MEM2 for raw FASTQ).
param.option: Auto (recommended)
strobealign
minimap2
BWA-MEM2
BWA

param.label: Enable local haplotype reassembly
param.help: Reassembles active regions around indels, soft-clipped alignments, and clustered variants to improve indel and complex variant accuracy.

param.label: Minimum mapping quality (MAPQ)
param.help: Reads with mapping quality below this cutoff are ignored during variant calling.

param.label: Minimum base quality (Phred)
param.help: Individual read bases with Phred quality below this cutoff are excluded from allele counts.

param.label: Minimum SNV quality score (QUAL)
param.help: Minimum Phred-scaled variant quality required to report a single-nucleotide variant.

param.label: Minimum indel quality score (QUAL)
param.help: Minimum Phred-scaled variant quality required to report an insertion or deletion.

param.name: dedup
param.label: PCR duplicate removal
param.help: Removes optical and PCR duplicate read pairs sharing identical alignment coordinates and template length. Set to Off for targeted PCR amplicon sequencing where distinct molecules share identical primer endpoints.
param.option: Automatic (remove duplicates and warn on amplicon-like libraries)
On (always remove PCR duplicates)
Off (keep all fragments for targeted PCR amplicon libraries)

tool.help:
**What this tool does**
**Focaloop VariationLoop** calls single-nucleotide variants (SNVs) and insertions/deletions (indels) for any organism from Galaxy paired-end FASTQ collections (`list:paired`), aligned BAM/CRAM datasets, or public SRA/ENA runs (using pre-assembled Logan unitigs when available). It handles both single samples and multi-sample cohorts natively, combining streaming alignment, optional host/off-target k-mer pre-filtering, compressed-block CRAM region slicing, local haplotype reassembly, and a compact `.focaloop.tar.zst` state bundle for instant downstream queries in **Focaloop Query**.
-----
**How it works**
1. **Automatic route selection:** Inspects your inputs and picks the most efficient engine automatically — pre-assembled Logan k=31 unitig streaming for available public SRA/ENA accessions, compressed-block `.crai` container slicing for indexed CRAM inputs, optional k-mer host/off-target pre-filtering for targeted or microbial/pathogen FASTQs, or direct diploid streaming alignment. 2. **Streaming alignment and duplicate filtering:** Maps paired reads (or unitigs) with the fastest working aligner on the server, deduplicates reads in-stream, and accumulates base and indel evidence in a low-memory paged pileup structure. 3. **Local haplotype reassembly and calling:** Reassembles active windows around candidate indels, soft-clips, and clustered variants before emitting a VCF v4.2 file (automatically merged across all samples in multi-sample cohorts) and a flat variant summary table. 4. **Reusable cohort state bundle:** Saves per-sample variant calls, group labels, and streaming telemetry into a `.focaloop.tar.zst` archive that **Focaloop Query** can analyze immediately (for example, allele-frequency and Fst contrasts between populations) without re-reading sequencing data.
-----
**Choosing an input source**
| Your data | Sequencing input source to choose | Sample names & output behavior | |---|---|---| | One or more paired-end samples in your History | **Paired-end FASTQ collection (list:paired)** | Element identifiers become sample names automatically. Runs one job and writes a single VCF (merged multi-sample VCF for cohorts) + cohort state bundle | | One or more aligned BAM or CRAM datasets | **Aligned BAM or CRAM file(s)** | Dataset names become sample names automatically. Indexed CRAM files automatically slice only the compressed containers overlapping your BED targets | | Public SRA/ENA runs or remote CRAM/FASTQ URLs | **Public SRA/ENA run accessions or remote cohort manifest** | Enter a flat accession list, organize accessions into population/condition groups inline, or upload a TSV/CSV manifest. Streams compact Logan unitigs automatically when available |
-----
**Inputs and manifest format**
Choose your reference genome using one of three sources:
- **Built-in Galaxy genome (CVMFS cache, default):** Pick from genomes pre-cached on this Galaxy server. - **Reference genome from your Galaxy History (FASTA):** Select a FASTA or gzip-compressed FASTA from your History. - **Fetch automatically by NCBI assembly accession:** Enter a RefSeq (`GCF_` prefix) or GenBank (`GCA_` prefix) assembly accession to download the genome FASTA automatically.
**How sample names work**
You never need to type a manual sample name. VariationLoop derives clean, VCF-compatible sample names automatically:
- From each pair's **element identifier** in a `list:paired` collection - From the **dataset name** of each BAM/CRAM file (automatically stripping `.bam` and `.cram` suffixes) - From the **run accession** when using the flat accession list or inline group builder - From the **`sample_id`** column when supplying a cohort TSV/CSV manifest
**Optional population or group metadata sheet (for `list:paired` or BAM/CRAM cohorts)**
To run population or group comparisons later in **Focaloop Query**, optionally attach a two-column TSV or CSV matching your collection/dataset names:
``` sample_id group isolate_A resistant isolate_B resistant isolate_C sensitive isolate_D sensitive ```
**Cohort manifest format (for remote URLs or custom cohort metadata)**
When choosing **Cohort manifest from Galaxy History (TSV or CSV)** under public/remote inputs, provide a tab- or comma-separated file with a header row:
| Column | Required | Description | |---|---|---| | `sample_id` | Yes | Unique sample name written to the VCF header, summary TSV, and HTML report | | `group` | Yes | Population, cohort, or condition label saved in the state bundle for **Focaloop Query** | | `source` | Yes | Public SRA/ENA run accession (`SRR`, `ERR`, or `DRR` prefix), remote CRAM URL, or remote R1 FASTQ URL | | `crai_uri` | Remote CRAM | URL to the matching `.crai` index file for compressed-block CRAM region slicing | | `mate2_url` | Remote paired FASTQ | URL to the reverse (R2) FASTQ file when `source` is an R1 FASTQ URL |
Example cohort manifest:
``` sample_id group source crai_uri sample_1 site_A RUN_ACCESSION_1 sample_2 site_B https://example.org/alignments/sample_2.cram https://example.org/alignments/sample_2.cram.crai ```
-----
**Key parameters**
- **Calling model (`--ploidy`) and minimum WSAF (`--min-wsaf`):** Choose **Haploid or mixed-clone mixture** for haploid pathogens, microbes, and viruses (haploid parasites, bacteria, viruses, fungi). Calls continuous within-sample allele fractions (`WSAF`, default floor `0.25`) using a sequencing-error likelihood ratio with no 50/50 diploid assumption, emitting haploid `GT=1` and per-sample `FORMAT/WSAF` (preserved across merged multi-sample VCFs and used directly for continuous Hudson Fst in **Focaloop Query**). Lower `--min-wsaf` to `0.10-0.15` to detect minor clones in polyclonal infections, or raise to `0.50` for major-allele-only calls. Choose **Diploid** for human, vertebrate, or diploid eukaryotic genomes (`0/1`, `1/1`, `1/2` alongside `FORMAT/WSAF`). - **Target regions (`--targets-bed`, optional):** 0-based BED file (`chrom`, `start`, `end`). Restricts variant calling, local haplotype reassembly, compressed CRAM block slicing, and k-mer pre-filtering to your regions of interest. - **Pre-assembled Logan unitig streaming (`--logan-mode`):** Enabled in **Automatic** mode for public SRA/ENA accessions. Uses compact pre-assembled unitig graphs (~10-20x smaller than raw reads) when available in Logan and falls back seamlessly to raw reads otherwise. - **Host and off-target pre-filtering (`--host-depletion-mode`):** Under **Automatic**, builds a fast 15-mer filter for Logan unitigs (up to 50 Mb target/reference) and a 31-mer filter for BED-targeted FASTQs (up to 45 Mb), while skipping pre-filtering on whole-genome FASTQ runs. - **Local haplotype reassembly (`--reassembly`):** Enabled by default. Reassembles active regions around indels and clustered variants before calling. - **Quality thresholds (`--min-mapq`, `--min-bq`, `--snv-min-qual`, `--indel-min-qual`):** Default MAPQ 20, Phred base quality 13, SNV QUAL 20, and indel QUAL 15 provide a balanced sensitivity/precision operating point across microbial, pathogen, and diploid eukaryotic genomes.
-----
**Outputs**
1. **Variant calls (`variants.vcf`):** Standard VCF v4.2 file with genotypes (`GT`), genotype quality (`GQ`), read depth (`DP`), allelic depths (`AD`), and per-sample within-sample allele fraction (`FORMAT/WSAF`). Automatically merged across all samples when running a multi-sample cohort. 2. **Variant summary table (`variants_summary.tsv`):** Flat tabular summary with one row per non-reference call (`sample_id`, `chrom`, `pos`, `ref`, `alt`, `kind`, `gt`, `gq`, `dp`, `ad_ref`, `ad_alt`, `wsaf`, `qual`, `source`). 3. **HTML report:** Self-contained visual summary showing per-sample alignment/streaming telemetry, wire-bytes/duplicate statistics, variant counts, and a preview table of called variants. 4. **State bundle (`variationloop_state.focaloop.tar.zst`):** Compact cohort state bundle ready for instant downstream population allele-frequency and Fst queries in **Focaloop Query**.
-----
**Tips and troubleshooting**
- **Single sample in a `list:paired` collection:** Use Galaxy's **Build List of Dataset Pairs** action to wrap one or more R1/R2 sample pairs into a `list:paired` collection before running VariationLoop. - **Target pre-filter memory cap exceeded:** The 31-mer raw-FASTQ pre-filter supports target spans up to 45 Mb. For large whole genomes, either provide a BED file covering your genes/panels of interest or leave **Host and off-target pre-filtering** on **Automatic** or **Off**. - **Logan unitigs unavailable for a newly deposited run:** Keep **Pre-assembled Logan unitig streaming** on **Automatic** so VariationLoop streams raw reads cleanly for any run not yet indexed in Logan. - **Reference contig naming:** Ensure contig names in your optional BED file and BAM/CRAM header match the selected reference genome (for example, `chr1` vs. `1`).
